title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer (Zenodo, v1.0.0)
note: Software record by Dresden Goehner (independent researcher). Code, plan, derived data and results for probabilistic load forecasts over four PJM cold events (2014, 2015 as official-error anchor only, 2017-18, 2022). Three forecasters x five conformal calibrators, day-ahead (primary) and 1-hour horizons. Says protocol and formulas were frozen before any result.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark (Zenodo): headline findings
note: Headlines: uncalibrated 90% intervals lose coverage inside the events; 0 of 18 cells pass the repair judgement when the calibrator is chosen without the target event; retrospective leave-one-event-out overstates the two temperature-stratified Mondrian calibrators' event coverage by 11.6 and 21.2 points against chronological evaluation. Links the GitHub repository at tag v1.0.0.

title: DresdenGman/PJM-Cold-Calibration-Benchmark (README)
note: MIT licence. Day-ahead quantile boosting covered 12.5% of 2014 vortex hours vs 65.7% over the 2014 evaluation period; gaps 14.3 points (2018) and 9.2 (2022), so the strictest planned form of J1 narrowly missed. Best single repair reached 0.583 coverage. PJM's own day-ahead forecasts under-called all four event peaks (1.3% to 6.6%). CPU stack: sklearn, lightgbm, scipy; seed 42.

title: code/RESULTS_RUN1.md: J1 and populations
note: Event windows: 72 h (2014), 264 h (2018), 96 h (2022). J1 verdict at day-ahead: does not hold as written (quantile boosting gap 53.2, 14.3, 9.2 points; bar was 10 in all three), though the other learners show the drop too (linear-tree LightGBM 59.0, 15.8, 31.6). Bootstrap ranges are labelled descriptive, not confidence intervals, and are wide (2014 uncalibrated 0.125, range 0.000-0.333).

title: code/RESULTS_RUN1.md: J2, J3 and deviations
note: J2: all six horizon x learner cells fail under leave-one-event-out selection and under the chronological variant. J3 (no pass/fail): day-ahead quantile boosting gaps average +11.6 (C2a) and +21.2 (C2b) points, but per-event signs vary (C2a: +45.8, +15.2, -26.0) and other learners show smaller or negative means. Lists deviations, incl. trimmed LightGBM settings and operationalised bars.

title: preregistration/FREEZE_PROTOCOL.md (v2 + Amendment A1, in Chinese)
note: Plan dated 5 Nov 2026: v1, revised to v2 and declared frozen the same evening, then Amendment A1 minutes later (split data three ways, two Mondrian variants, leave-one-event-out calibrator selection), stating no Run-1 result existed yet. Defines J1, J2, J3 and a fallback if J2 fails. Day-ahead arm uses realised ERA5 weather, so it is an oracle-weather result. Aimed at Applied Energy.

title: Commit history of DresdenGman/PJM-Cold-Calibration-Benchmark
note: The public history is a single commit (74d631c, 6 Nov 2026) that adds the plan, the code and the results together, with one tag (v1.0.0). The freeze on 5 Nov therefore cannot be confirmed from a public timestamp earlier than the results; it rests on the author's statement. 0 stars, 0 forks, one contributor.

title: DATA_SOURCES.md
note: Load: EIA-930 demand for the PJM balancing authority as a whole (2018 and 2022 eras) and PJM metered load 2010-2014 (table not redistributed). Weather: ERA5 via the Open-Meteo archive, equal-weight mean of 15 grid points over the footprint; temperature, dew point, wind. Both horizons use realised weather. No zonal series; EIA-930 runs 0.5-0.7% above PJM metered load.

title: Bayesian Transformer for Probabilistic Load Forecasting in Smart Grids (named by you-research, not fetched)
note: Related work, not a replication: a different model and evaluation on PJM and other grids reports near-nominal 90% coverage in cold-snap subsets while a deterministic baseline falls to about two thirds. Different data, events and design, so it neither confirms nor contradicts this benchmark. Known only from the research call's source list.
